aria: Animated recap of the Pelicans' 105 to 104 win at the Clippers: Trey Murphy III's driving floater with 42 seconds left that made it 104 to 99, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Zion Williamson's 25 points, the top scorers, how the Pelicans won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from Hoops Nightly's game page for the Pelicans' 105–104 win at the Clippers on Nov 27, 2026, the last NBA Cup group game for both teams; Digest Sports and CBS Sports show the same player lines. All 105 New Orleans points and all 104 L.A. points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (39 of 88, 7 of 30 from three, 20 of 26 FT for New Orleans; 36 of 91, 13 of 45, 19 of 25 for L.A.), rebounds (53–46), assists (26–25), steals (12–7) and blocks (3–6). The quarter scores (29–25–26–25 to 28–22–27–27) are on Hoops Nightly, Digest Sports and CBS Sports; 54–50 at the half and 80–77 after three are in Fastbreak Journal. Points in the paint (64–34), fast-break points (18–10) and second-chance points (14–25) are from Hoops Nightly only; bench points (35–27) add up from the box. The biggest leads (New Orleans 7, L.A. 12) are on Hoops Nightly, and Digest Sports also has the Clippers' 12. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III each scored 25, and Murphy had 6 steals (AP via FOX Sports). The win ended New Orleans' four-game losing streak, and the Clippers have lost six straight; both teams finished NBA Cup group play 1–3 (AP). The finish: Darius Garland's three at 1:02 cut it to 102–99, Murphy's floater made it 104–99, Brandon Ingram's layup at 0:34 made it 104–101, Herbert Jones made one of two free throws with 9 seconds left, and Brook Lopez's 29-foot three at the horn made it 105–104 (CBS Sports play-by-play; Fastbreak Journal). Dejounte Murray (ankle) and Bradley Beal (knee) were out (Fastbreak Journal). Next: New Orleans visits Portland and the Clippers visit Golden State, both on Sunday (AP; Fastbreak Journal; Hoops Nightly).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Trey Murphy III's floater with 42.3 seconds left that made it 104–99: CBS Sports' play-by-play has a "two point driving floating jump shot" at 0:42 with the assist from Zion Williamson, Fastbreak Journal a 5-foot floater from Williamson with 42.3 seconds left, and Digest Sports "Murphy's floater made it 104-99." So the board's Pelicans +3 to +5 is 102–99 to 104–99. The defender isn't described, so it is drawn as the template's plain drive to a short finish. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the New Orleans Pelicans or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Murphy's listed 6-foot-8 and 206 pounds (Basketball-Reference; Wikipedia), in the Pelicans' road kit with No. 25 (Basketball-Reference). No wingspan is reported, so his arms are at the default length. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
